approved: Argued that the Right to Protest Bill 2025 would protect peaceful protest as a federally protected right, limit restrictions to narrowly defined circumstances, and invalidate disproportionate state or territory penalties; debate was adjourned.

Presented the Right to Protest Bill 2025, arguing that it would protect peaceful assembly and protest by incorporating rights from the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and reversing what was described as an erosion of protest rights and increasing legal suppression in Australia.

Moved to suspend standing orders and restore the Australian Education Legislation Amendment (Prohibiting the Indoctrination of Children) Bill 2020 and twelve other listed bills to the Notice Paper for consideration at the second reading stage; both questions were agreed to.

Moved that the Right to Protest Bill 2025 be considered today and the Members of Parliament (Staff) Amendment (Providing Certainty and Improving Integrity) Bill 2025 be considered on Thursday, 28 August 2025.
